sources.title: SOP (two fragments supplied: sections 2 and 7)
sources.summary: Only two sentences were supplied. Section 2: the department manager approves. Section 7: only the finance director approves. Process name, start and end conditions, service levels, evidence and exceptions were not supplied.

groups.name: Department managers
groups.purpose: Approver named in SOP section 2. Candidate assignee of the decision «Decide on the request» if decision D1 resolves in favour of section 2 or a two-step approval.

flags.detail: The source does not say which department manager: the requester's own manager (a per-case owner) or a fixed group. See decision D4.

groups.name: Finance director
groups.purpose: Approver named in SOP section 7 («only the finance director approves»). Candidate assignee of the decision «Decide on the request» if decision D1 resolves in favour of section 7 or a two-step approval.

flags.detail: One named position. A group is proposed so ownership survives absences; the delegate is decision D5.

workflows.name: Request approval

access.note: The source does not say who opens a request, who owns the design or how sensitive the cases are. No grant is proposed until decision D3 names the starters; `creator_only` is a placeholder, not a design choice. Sensitivity `internal` is an assumption.

actions.name: Prepare the request for approval
evidence: Supporting documents attached to the case
actions.description:
Task: Describe the request so the approver can decide on it.
How: 1. Fill `request_summary` with what is requested and why. 2. Add the supporting detail in `justification`. 3. Attach any document that supports the request to the case. 4. Complete the action to send the request for decision.
Evidence: `request_summary` filled; supporting documents attached to the case.
Done when: The summary and the justification are complete and the action is completed.
Exceptions: If the request was returned for rework, read the approver's comment, correct the request and complete the action again. If the request is no longer needed, say so in a comment so the approver can reject it.

actions.name: Decide on the request
evidence: Mandatory comment on «Return for rework» and «Reject»
actions.description:
Task: Decide whether the request described in `request_summary` may proceed.
How: 1. Read `request_summary`, `justification` and the attached documents. 2. Check the request against the criteria of the procedure that applies to it. 3. Choose «Approve», «Return for rework» or «Reject».
Evidence: A comment with the reason is mandatory on «Return for rework» and «Reject».
Done when: The decision is recorded with the required comment.
Exceptions: If the information is insufficient to decide, choose «Return for rework» and list what is missing. If the procedure designates another person to approve this request, do not decide: comment who must decide and choose «Return for rework» so the request is routed to that person.

setupNotes: Action `decide` has no assignee: SOP section 2 names the department manager and section 7 names only the finance director. Assign it only after decision D1 is resolved; if the resolution is a two-step approval, the design gains a second decision action and must be re-run through provia-workflow-designer.
Groups `department_managers` and `finance_director` are proposals derived from the two sentences supplied; neither has members or an area yet.
No service level was supplied: `due` is unset on both actions (decision D6).

The `prepare` action, the fields `request_summary` and `justification`, and the «Return for rework» and «Reject» branches are recommendations: the source contains no intake, rejection or rework step (decisions D2 and D7).

decisions.question: Who approves the request? SOP section 2 says the department manager approves; section 7 says only the finance director approves. Possible resolutions: (a) section 7 supersedes section 2 (one decision by the finance director); (b) section 2 applies and section 7 is an error or a different process (one decision by the department manager); (c) both apply in sequence (department manager, then finance director: two decision actions); (d) each applies to a different scope, for example an amount band or a request category the fragments do not mention. The designer did not choose.
decisions.owner: Process owner / author of the SOP

decisions.question: What is the request being approved, what starts a case and what ends it? Only the two approval sentences were supplied; the workflow name «Request approval», the fields `request_summary` and `justification` and the `prepare` action are placeholders.
Who may open a request (create_incident: every employee, a team, or a named group) and which group owns the workflow design (edit)? The manifest declares `creator_only` until this is answered.

If the department manager approves (D1 a/c/d): is it the requester's own department manager, chosen per case, or a fixed group of managers? A per-case owner needs a `user` field on the case with `assigneeRef: field:<key>` and a fallback group, which the product cannot assign automatically yet.
Who decides in the finance director's absence? Section 7 says «only the finance director», so a delegate would change the rule and must be confirmed by the process owner.
What is the service level for the decision and for preparing the request? No deadline was supplied; `due` stays unset until one is stated.
Does the procedure allow «Reject» (case cancelled) and «Return for rework» (back to the requester)? Both branches are recommendations; the source gives only the approval.
Country, language, currency and timezone of the organization. Angola, English, AOA and Africa/Luanda are provisional; no country was supplied.
